profile.name: Benjamin
profile.headline: I build small, dependable systems — from database schema to the interface you actually touch.
profile.summary: Software engineer working across backend and frontend. Currently focused on data-heavy products, developer tooling, and keeping things simple enough to maintain.

items.title: Ledger Lab
items.descriptionLong:
Ledger Lab is a bookkeeping sandbox I built to learn double-entry accounting properly. You record transactions against accounts, and every view — trial balance, general ledger, profit and loss — is derived from the same append-only journal.

- Append-only journal: no updates, only compensating entries
- Replayable state: any balance can be rebuilt from the log at a chosen point in time
- Unit tests written against hand-checked example ledgers

The whole persistence layer is one migrations file, and the UI never computes a balance itself — it asks the journal.
items.summaryShort: A double-entry bookkeeping sandbox with an append-only journal and replayable state.
bullets: Built an append-only journal with compensating entries and full state replay from any point in the log.
Wrote the balance engine as pure TypeScript with unit tests against hand-checked example ledgers.

items.title: Signal Desk
items.descriptionLong:
Signal Desk collapses noisy monitoring alerts into a single ranked queue, so an on-call engineer reads one list instead of five channels.

Ranking is intentionally boring: severity, then blast radius, then age. The queue holds no state of its own — it is recomputed from raw events, so it can be rebuilt after an outage without losing anything.
items.summaryShort: A triage queue that turns noisy monitoring events into one ranked list for on-call.
bullets: Replaced stateless alert fan-out with a single derived queue recomputed from raw events.
Kept ranking rules explicit and testable so on-call could reason about ordering.

items.title: Atlas API
items.descriptionLong:
Atlas is a versioned REST API and TypeScript SDK for an offline-first field data collection tool. Devices queue writes while offline; the server reconciles them by revision.

The interesting part was conflict handling: every record carries a monotonic revision, and a write that loses the race goes back to the client with the current server state instead of being silently dropped.
items.summaryShort: A versioned REST API and typed SDK with revision-based conflict handling for offline clients.
bullets: Designed revision-based conflict resolution so queued offline writes are rejected explicitly, never silently lost.
Generated the typed client SDK and OpenAPI description from a single schema source.
